_about: Where a campaign begins (rules/openings.py; docs/design-c-starts.md). One document per start.

fits: which characters and towns it suits. backgrounds = written for them (drawn six times as often); favours = a multiplier for a background on an open start; open = anybody may draw it; scales, needs (alternatives joined by |), people (own, stranger, any).

where: at = place | lodging | road | outskirts, and for a place the kinds of place it can stand in. Road and outskirts starts stand the party on the settlement's own road heads or outskirts (Lane B's ring); they live in road-starts.json.

lead: the person who speaks first. label is their name on the board (two or three words, 'the ...'); look is how they are seen; says is what they say. Whoever the world casts brings their own name, face and pronouns, so nothing here says he or she.

incident: bring (somebody into the scene), wound (hurt, staggered or dying, the damage worked out from their own hit points by rule), fight (spawn and roll initiative; from: land draws the attackers from what the ground holds in the bestiary, at the party's level). Every number is the engine's.
hand_off: where the player takes over. The opening stops on `moment` and never narrates past it.
No document names a place, a person or a people, and none carries a digit: the world's names are filled in when the start is staged.

starts.name: Called to the cage
starts.doing: You are pushing through a ring of people who do not want to give up their places.
starts.edge: In the cleared space at the middle a fighter lies where the last blow put them, and the crowd has gone quiet in the wrong way.

lead.label: the cage owner
lead.look: talking over a shoulder the whole way, one hand clearing the crowd
lead.says: Went down in the second and has not got up. The last one who looked wanted paying first, and I am not paying twice.

hand_off.moment: The cage owner stops at the edge of the cleared ground and steps back to let you through.

starts.errand: You came because somebody sent a runner for the bonesetter, and you are the bonesetter.
suggestions: Kneel and stop the bleeding
Ask the cage owner what happened
Clear the crowd back first

grants.say: You know the look of somebody with a cracked skull.

starts.name: Pulled from the water
starts.doing: You have your sleeves still wet to the elbow from the hauling.
starts.edge: Somebody who went into the water has just been dragged out of it, grey in the face, and is not breathing well.

lead.label: the boatman
lead.look: soaked to the waist and shouting for room
lead.says: Went in off the edge and came up once. You know water, you know what to do with somebody full of it.

hand_off.moment: The boatman lets go of the collar and sits back on the wet stones, looking at you.

starts.errand: You came down to the water for work on the crossings, the only trade you have ever had.
suggestions: Turn them over and get the water out
Tell the boatman to fetch a blanket
Ask who saw them go in

grants.say: You know how this water runs, and where it takes what falls in.

starts.name: The bout
starts.doing: You are standing in the ring you were paid to stand in, with the bets still being called.
starts.edge: Your opponent has stepped in early, before the bell, and the crowd likes it.

lead.label: the bookmaker
lead.look: on a crate at the ring's edge, chalk on both hands
lead.says: No bell tonight. The money is down and the other side is not waiting. Fists only, and the one standing gets paid.

hand_off.moment: The bookmaker drops the chalk and steps down off the crate.

starts.errand: You came for the purse the bout pays, which is rent and food for a month.
suggestions: Put the challenger down, with fists only
Keep my guard up and see what they have
Tell the bookmaker this was not the deal

starts.name: Short on the gate
starts.doing: You are on the gate again, a spear's length from where you stood last season.
starts.edge: Somebody has just come through without stopping, and a carter is on the ground shouting about a slashed purse.

lead.label: the sergeant
lead.look: red in the face and pointing up the street
lead.says: That one, in the grey hood, the one not running yet. We are two short on this gate and you know the faces. Bring them back.

hand_off.moment: The sergeant turns back to the carter and leaves the street to you.

starts.errand: You came back to the gate because it is the one place that ever paid you regular.
suggestions: Go after the hooded runner
Shout for them to stop
Ask the carter what was taken

starts.name: The name on the list
starts.doing: You are holding a paper with a description on it that fits half the street.
starts.edge: Across the way, the face the paper describes has just looked up and seen you looking.

lead.label: the informant
lead.look: at your elbow, not looking at anybody
lead.says: By the far stall, the one with the bad ear. Has seen you now, so it is running or talking, and my part is done.

hand_off.moment: The informant is gone into the crowd before you can turn round.

starts.errand: You came for the price on this one, which somebody is holding for whoever brings them in.
suggestions: Walk straight over and take hold
Cut round behind the stalls
Call out that I only want to talk

starts.name: A hand short
starts.doing: You are looking over the wagons with the eye of somebody who has walked beside them.
starts.edge: One wagon stands half loaded with nobody at the traces, and its owner is asking everybody in reach the same question.

lead.label: the wagon master
lead.look: a tally stick in one fist and dust to the knees
lead.says: Lost a driver this morning and the wagons leave at first light. You have done this before, it shows. The work pays at the far end.

hand_off.moment: The wagon master holds out the tally stick and waits for an answer.

starts.errand: You came looking for a place on a train going somewhere, because walking the road alone is how people vanish.
suggestions: Ask where the wagons are bound
Ask what happened to the last driver
Take the tally stick

starts.name: Home by the back door
starts.doing: You have come in through the kitchen the way you always did, and the noise from the front is the wrong kind.
starts.edge: A drinker who will not pay has a stool in both hands and has already put the potboy on the floor.

lead.label: the cook
lead.look: in the kitchen doorway with a ladle held like a club
lead.says: Will not pay and will not go, and nobody out there is going to make them. You grew up throwing drunks out of this room.

hand_off.moment: The drunk sees you, and swings the stool round to face the new trouble.

starts.errand: You came home for a bed and a meal you would not have to pay for.
suggestions: Take the stool off the drunk
Get between the drunk and the potboy
Talk the drunk down

starts.name: Stop, thief
starts.doing: You are standing at a stall with your hands empty and nothing bought yet.
starts.edge: The cash box on the stall is open and empty, and every face nearby has turned to you.

lead.label: the stallholder
lead.look: with a hand clamped on your sleeve
lead.says: That is the one. Stood right here while the box went. Turn out your pockets or somebody fetches the watch.

hand_off.moment: The stallholder's grip does not loosen, and somebody at the back has started calling for the watch.

starts.errand: You came to buy what you need for the road with the little money you have.
suggestions: Turn out my pockets
Point out who was standing behind me
Pull free and walk away

grants.say: A stallholder has named you a thief in front of the market.

starts.name: Sent for
starts.doing: You are standing in front of a door with a message in your hand asking you to come here, and nothing else in it.
starts.edge: The people coming out of the door are not talking to each other, and one of them looks back at you as though you are expected.

lead.label: the steward
lead.look: with the door held half open and a list in the other hand
lead.says: You took your time. The one who sent for you is inside and does not like waiting. Come in or go, but decide here.

hand_off.moment: The steward holds the door and looks at you.

starts.errand: You came because a message said you should, and the message was paid for.
suggestions: Go inside
Ask who sent for me
Ask what this is about

starts.name: Cutpurse
starts.doing: You are wedged in the press of the crowd, a hand on your belt out of habit.
starts.edge: Your belt is lighter than it was, and a small figure is ducking away under the awnings.

lead.label: the fishmonger
lead.says: Your purse. The small one had it off you, going under the awning there. Quick, or it is gone.

hand_off.moment: The cutpurse looks back once from the end of the row.

starts.errand: You came to eat something hot and find out who in this place is hiring.
suggestions: Go after the cutpurse
Shout for somebody to stop them
Let it go and count what is left

starts.name: Trouble in the lane
starts.doing: You took the short way through, the way anybody would who did not know better.
starts.edge: Two figures have stepped out of a doorway ahead with cudgels, and somebody with a basket is backed against the wall between you and them.

lead.label: the basket carrier
lead.look: pressed flat to the wall, eyes on you
lead.says: They want what I carry, and now they will have yours as well. Do not just stand there.

hand_off.moment: The nearer of the two lifts a cudgel and comes on.

starts.errand: You came to find a bed before dark, and a cheap one.
suggestions: Stand in front of the basket carrier
Go for the nearer robber
Tell them to take their chances somewhere else

starts.name: A room and a notice
starts.doing: You have just come in off the road and put your pack down by the door.
starts.edge: A notice pinned by the hearth offers pay for work nobody in the room will look at.

lead.label: the innkeeper
lead.look: wiping the same cup for the third time
lead.says: There is a room if you can pay for it tonight, and there is work on that notice if you cannot. Most cannot.

hand_off.moment: The innkeeper sets the cup down and waits.

starts.errand: You came in off the road for a bed, and the purse is thinner than the road was long.
suggestions: Ask about the notice
Ask the price of the room
Ask why nobody will look at the notice

starts.name: The hiring table
starts.doing: You are in the line at a trestle table where somebody is taking names.
starts.edge: The person ahead of you was turned away without a word, and the table has gone through three pages already.

lead.label: the guild clerk
lead.look: with ink to the wrists and a page nearly full
lead.says: Hands wanted for the week, fed and paid at the end of it. Can you carry, count or fight? Say which and say it quickly.

hand_off.moment: The guild clerk dips the pen and holds it over the page.

starts.errand: You came for a week's paid work, before your money runs out.
suggestions: Say I can fight
Ask what the work is
Ask what it pays

starts.name: The bread stall
starts.doing: You are haggling over yesterday's bread, and losing.
starts.edge: Two stalls down, a trader has started packing up again, and the ones either side are watching rather than asking.

lead.label: the bread seller
lead.look: at the bread stall, arms folded
lead.says: Yesterday's is yesterday's price. That one down there, packing up, that is the third this week.

hand_off.moment: The bread seller looks past you, down the row.

starts.errand: You came to sell what you carried in and buy a week's food with the money.
suggestions: Ask why the trader is packing up
Go and see for myself
Keep to what I came here for

starts.name: The common room
starts.doing: You have a bowl in front of you and half of it left.
starts.edge: The clatter nearest the door has died, and the hush is spreading inward one table at a time.

lead.label: the potboy
lead.look: clearing the next table and not hurrying
lead.says: Eat up. Whoever that is at the door, it is not the kind of trouble that pays for its bowl.

hand_off.moment: The potboy stops clearing and looks at the door with everybody else.

starts.errand: You came for a meal you could afford and the name of somebody who hires.
suggestions: Look at the door
Ask the potboy who it is
Finish my bowl

starts.name: The well queue
starts.doing: You are third in line with an empty bucket.
starts.edge: The queue has stopped moving, and whatever is being said at the front of it is not being repeated back down the line.

lead.label: the old neighbour
lead.look: ahead of you in the line, leaning on a stick
lead.says: Something at the front. Always something at the front, this week. You new, or just thirsty?

hand_off.moment: The old neighbour turns round properly to look at you.

starts.errand: You came for water, and to hear where a stranger can sleep tonight.
suggestions: Ask what is going on at the front
Go up the line and see
Keep my place and wait
